summary: Busy earnings and event tape. IDXX (held) reported this morning with a beat and raise and is up about 20%, which resolves the 11-02 flag in its favor. AAPL reports after the close today (company-scheduled, per Benzinga and TradingView), CLX's estimated date is also today with no results yet, and a cluster of prints lands inside the 5-day window: MTCH, ULS and GPOR (11-03, estimates), SMG (11-04), and CARG, TPR, RL, ONC and DBX (11-05). Crypto is stabilising after the Binance hack (withdrawals resuming, 90% of losses replaced, no exchange failure on this evidence), while the macro tape carries the Tuesday midterms, the Iran war and Brent near $111, last Friday's chip rout, and October NFP later in the week.

Options imply a move to about $355. The Mag 7 AI-capex selloff makes the print a read on the whole group.

Aftermath of the record $6.3B Binance hack: Binance replaced 90% of the stolen funds from company money, said it completed new security upgrades and resumed withdrawals in phases (next phase Tuesday), the FBI blames North Korea, and the Secret Service is investigating with Circle and others. BTC held its ground (Bitcoin outperformed gold last week). On the news alone the 'exchange failure' invalidation clause has not tripped: Binance is paying users back and reopening withdrawals, not failing. Open risks: the hack's DeFi lending spillover, Coinbase/Robinhood/Gemini stocks falling, a CFTC push to register exchanges (a regulatory shift, not yet a rule), Strategy resuming purchases (811 BTC, $65.5M) after its pause but facing the MSCI exclusion decision on 11-11, Circle earnings 11-04 before the open, and the midterms Tuesday (an analyst warns of a post-midterm correction). Nothing here is a hard regulatory or exchange failure.

Tagged on the Binance coverage (the hack reportedly involved borrowing Ether against stablecoins). Bitmine added 8,573 ETH and held firm, but ETH ETFs posted their worst monthly outflows on record in October and a head-and-shoulders pattern is cited. Relative weakness thread unchanged; no ETH-specific rule.

Futures were up Monday ahead of Apple and Palantir earnings. Midterms Tuesday and the Iran war (Brent about $111, Trump saying it ends 'one way or the other') add event risk. Bullish counterweights are seasonal (S&P up 19 of 19 in midterm Nov-April windows).

notable.headline: IDEXX Q3 EPS $4.01 beats $3.71; FY26 EPS guide raised to $14.96-$15.16 vs $14.82 est; stock about +20%
notable.read: Held name. Clean beat and raise resolves the print risk that the 10-29 and 10-30 flags and the stale thesis premise (L5) pointed at; the PT cuts (Jefferies, UBS) that preceded it were wrong-footed. The move is large enough that the entry-relative position and any stop distance have changed materially, which is a sizing question for others, not a news one.

notable.headline: Apple reports fiscal Q4 after the close today; BofA cuts FY27 iPhone forecast by 9M units; J595 home robot may slip to 2028
notable.read: Print is today, so the date question is closed. The pre-print read is two-sided: demand evidence for iPhone Duo and the 'avoids the AI spending binge' narrative against component costs and a lowered unit forecast. Options imply a large move. Most other AAPL-tagged items (Musk, Tesla weekly, prediction-market previews, macro roundups) are noise.

notable.headline: BMO raises Cheniere PT to $350; senior notes due 2037 offered; WSJ: US pushes to restore Russian gas to Europe via Ukraine
notable.read: PT drift keeps rising after the 10-29 beat and dividend raise. The notes offering is refinancing. The Russian gas report is a long-dated competitive risk to US LNG and is only a headline so far.

notable.headline: Rothschild & Co Redburn lowers Adobe PT to $140 from $270
notable.read: A cut of nearly half on a single name is rare and fits the AI-disruption rout in software and chips. The rest of the ADBE items are filler. No filing or earnings event until 12-09, so this is a sentiment signal only.

notable.headline: Domino's lowers fiscal 2026 U.S. store-opening target and operating income growth outlook (fiscal.ai, dated 10-30)
notable.read: Held name. If new, this is a guidance cut on top of the 10-26 DA Davidson PT cut and the surviving class action. The only source is an aggregator summary linked to a Zacks comparison piece, and no 8-K is in the window, so it may echo the 10-20 results. Worth checking whether it reflects a new disclosure.

notable.headline: Binance finishes security upgrades, resumes withdrawals in phases; replaces 90% of stolen crypto; FBI blames North Korea
notable.read: The incident is moving from crisis to cleanup. Withdrawals are reopening and 98% of users stayed, so an exchange failure is not evidenced. Continues the 10-30 flag, which has so far come to less than feared on price (BTC about flat through the weekend). Follow-through to watch: Tuesday's withdrawal phase, exchange-stock weakness, and any CFTC move toward a federal registration option.

notable.headline: Strategy buys 811 BTC for $65.5M after pausing; MSCI to announce index exclusion rules on 11-11 with Strategy a named candidate
notable.read: Ends the 10-27 purchase pause but at a small size, and sets a dated passive-selling risk for the biggest treasury holder (a headline cites about $2.8B of potential passive selling). The 10-28 Datavault credibility hit and Strategy strain thread continues; this is the first dated catalyst.

notable.read: Continues and deepens the AI-capex thread (Alphabet, Amazon, Intel). Hard price damage now, not just worry. Futures bounced Monday, so Apple and Palantir prints and the midterms are the next tests.
